title: Same Claim, Different Judgment: Benchmarking Scenario-Induced Bias in Multilingual Financial Misinformation Detection

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing F1 scores for financial misinformation detection between scenario-agnostic baselines and prompts conditioned on specific investor roles and behavioral finance traits (overconfidence, loss aversion, herding, anchoring, confirmation bias).

Measuring the deviation in model verification performance (F1 scores) when conditioned on different regional financial market contexts (e.g., Europe, USA, Asia Pacific, China Mainland, UAE) compared to a baseline.
Evaluating changes in F1 scores when the LLM is prompted with different ethnic backgrounds (e.g., American, Chinese, Indian, Arab, Latino/Hispanic, African) combined with specific investor roles.
Evaluating changes in F1 scores when the LLM is prompted with different religious beliefs (e.g., Christianity, Islam, Buddhism, Judaism) combined with specific investor roles.

Comparing financial misinformation detection performance (accuracy and F1 scores) and the magnitude of behavioral biases across high-resource (English, Chinese) and low-resource (Greek, Bengali) languages.
Measuring differences in model judgment and bias manifestations when prompted with distinct financial decision-maker roles (Retail Investor, Professional, Company Owner).
